newsitem.title: UK: Russia's next Eurobond not due before June-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Russia's next Eurobond not due before June-dealers.

text.p: Russia's second dollar Eurobond will not be launched until June at the earliest as it awaits improved investor sentiment, bankers said on Thursday.
"Russia's bond will not come before June," a banker familiar with the transaction said.
"By that time, market sentiment (for emerging market debt) may have improved because the May FOMC meeting will have decided on interest rate moves," he said.

Earlier this week, Russia said it would issue its second dollar Eurobond soon via J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg. The deal would have a maturity of at least five years, first deputy prime minister Anatoly Chubais said.
Russia first tapped the international capital markets last November with a heavily oversubscribed $1.0 billion five-year bond. In March it issued a 2.0 billion mark seven-year bond.
Since then, appetite for emerging market debt has dropped sharply on the back of a volatile U.S. Treasury market. U.S. interest rates were increased to 5.50 percent from 5.25 percent in March.
A further rise could come at the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting if inflationary pressures are seen to be building up in the U.S. economy.
"There is a bit of negative investor psychology towards emerging markets," a debt trader at a U.S. bank said. "They want to see stability in the underlying Treasury market before committing funds."
Russia hopes to extend its borrowing maturity in the dollar sector, bankers said, but whether it will be able to do so depends on the state of the market.
"A seven-year bond would make sense, because traditionally borrowers go from five-, to seven-, to ten-year maturities," a debt trader at a European bank said.

"(But) a seven-year deal is impossible in the current market environment. If the deal does not take place until the autumn, then things may change. For now, I would assume it will be a five-year deal," he said.
Russia's 9.25 percent 2001 bond was trading at around 300 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, in from a 345 b.p. launch spread.
Its seven-year mark bond was quoted at around 390 b.p. over from a 370 b.p. launch spread.
The size of the forthcoming issue is also uncertain, bankers said. A deal for at least $500 million was expected, with a maximum of $1.0 billion.
Russia may decide trade off a smaller size for a longer maturity, or issue a larger but shorter-dated bond, they said.
Russia has said it plans to borrow at least another $2.0 billion this year, and needs the money to cover its budget deficit.

Chubais on Thursday said Russia's 1997 budget was unrealistic because tax revenues were lower than expected and said he would cut spending and raise over $5.0 billion through state sell-offs and precious metal sales
The next capital markets transaction out of Russia is expected to be the City of Moscow's debut Eurobond via CSFB and Nomura.

Roadshows for the deal are due to start on May 12, dealers said, and would likely last two weeks. Launch was expected at the end of May, and the deal's size was seen around $500 million, with a three- or five-year maturity, they said.
"Moscow's bond is expected next," the U.S. bank's trader said. "It will be closely watched by Russia as it is an important test for the market's ability to absorb new issues."
A slew of other Russian borrowers are waiting to raise funds abroad, including the City of St Petersburg, the Nizhny Novgorod region, companies like LUKoil and Gazprom and a number of Russian banks.
